courses.title: Advanced Health Data Analytics
courses.source_title: ADVANCED HEALTH DATA ANALYTICS
courses.school: School of Public Health and Social Sciences
courses.summary: The Advanced Health Data Analytics course is designed to equip academics, data practitioners, and health professionals with state-of-the-art analytical skills for the rapidly evolving field of digital health. The course focuses on the practical application of cutting-edge technologies, including machine learning, artificial intelligence (AI), sophisticated data visualisation, and automated analytics tools, to transform complex health data into actionable insights, building on fundamental analytics expertise. To support policy development, clinical decision support, disease surveillance, and health system performance improvement, participants will gain practical experience applying advanced analytics to real-world health datasets.
courses.duration: The course will be conducted over five (5) days, with a total of 40 contact hours, combining lectures, hands-on practical sessions, group work, and applied projects.
courses.target_audience: Participants should have prior training or experience in basic health data analytics, statistics, or programming (e.g., completion of Introduction to Health Data Analytics or an equivalent course).
courses.learning_outcomes: . By the end of the course, participants will be able to: Apply advanced data cleaning and transformation techniques Perform exploratory and inferential analysis on health datasets Develop and evaluate basic machine learning models for health applications Design advanced dashboards and visual analytics Translate analytical results into policy- and practice-relevant insights

courses.summary: This module provides participants with an in-depth understanding of applied entrepreneurship, emphasizing the practical aspects of establishing, managing, and expanding a business both within Tanzania and internationally. It draws upon case studies of entrepreneurs’ successes, challenges, setbacks, and strategic shifts, while examining sector-specific opportunities and effective approaches for innovation, resilience, and sustainable growth. The module is designed to address critical gaps in the Tanzanian entrepreneurship ecosystem: Limited access to finance → participants engage in simulations and sessions with financiers to practice fundraising and financial decision-making.
courses.duration: One week (five days) 2.3 Course objectives Develop Applied Entrepreneurial Skills – Enable participants to translate ideas into viable business ventures through hands-on learning in sales, marketing, human resource management, financial planning, and applied entrepreneurship practices, highlighting their role in job creation and economic transformation. Identify and Exploit Opportunities – Train learners to spot local and global market gaps, apply design thinking, problem-solving, and innovation
courses.target_audience: Minimum diploma or undergraduate degree in a health or related field. Non-health or health related field with relevant work experience.
courses.learning_outcomes: . At the end of the module, participants will be able to: Define applied entrepreneurship and explain its contribution to job creation and economic transformation. Identify and evaluate entrepreneurial opportunities across sectors such as health, nutrition ICT such as telehealth, AI etc., pharmaceutical, manufacturing, and the green economy. Apply design thinking, problem-solving, and innovation tools to address real business challenges. Critically analyze case studies of Tanzanian and international entrepreneurs to extract lessons from successes, challenges, setbacks, and strategic shifts, Formulate practical strategies to access finance, markets, and mentorship. Use digital tools and platforms to strengthen enterprise operations and growth. Pitch a viable business idea to peers and practicing entrepreneurs for feedback and improvement.

courses.title: BIOMEDICAL AND PHARMACEUTICAL SCIENCES BRIDGING COURSE FOR PHARMACY GRADUATES
courses.source_title: BIOMEDICAL AND PHARMACEUTICAL SCIENCES BRIDGING COURSE FOR PHARMACY GRADUATES
courses.summary: This is a targeted multidisciplinary CPD bridging course for pharmacy graduates who obtained their BPharm degree through a lateral-entry route after prior diploma-level pharmacy training, particularly the three-year lateral-entry BPharm pathway used by the target graduates in India. In the lateral-entry system, prior diploma learning is recognized and the student joins the degree programme at an advanced level rather than repeating all foundational content. When the training background of these graduates was considered in relation to the four-year BPharm programme used in Tanzania, the Pharmacy Council highlighted specific gaps in selected basic biomedical and pharmaceutical sciences.
courses.duration: The course will be delivered over eight (8) weeks in an intensive modular/block format. Training will normally be conducted five days per week, with approximately 10 learning hours per day, giving 50 learning hours per week and an overall course workload of approximately 400 learning hours.
courses.target_audience: The primary target participants are pharmacy graduates who first completed diploma-level pharmacy training and subsequently obtained a recognized BPharm degree through a lateral-entry route, particularly the three-year lateral-entry BPharm pathway in India. Participants should have documented evidence that bridging is required because one or more of the biomedical or pharmaceutical science areas covered by this course were identified as missing or insufficiently covered during qualification review. The Pharmacy Council's assessment and/or review of the applicant's academic records may be used to confirm the need for the bridging course.
courses.learning_outcomes: Upon completion of the course, participants should be able to: • Relate the structure of the human body to normal physiological function and selected clinical conditions. • Explain key biochemical and molecular processes involved in health, disease and drug action. • Apply fundamental inorganic and organic chemistry principles to pharmaceutical substances, reactions, synthesis and analysis. • Explain major mechanisms of cell injury, inflammation, tissue repair, haemodynamic disturbance, neoplasia and selected organ-system diseases. • Describe and apply basic pharmaceutical analytical and quality-control principles, including volumetric, spectroscopic and chromatographic methods. • Integrate anatomy, physiology, biochemistry and pathology to explain the pathophysiology of selected common disease states. • Demonstrate safe, accurate, ethical and evidence-informed practice during laboratory, case-based and collaborative learning activities.
courses.certificate_awarded: Participants who successfully complete the approved course requirements will receive a Certificate of Completion issued by DCEPD.

courses.summary: This five-day short course aims to provide a practical foundation in data analysis and use for health supply chain management, focusing on transforming routine logistics data into actionable intelligence. It covers the full data lifecycle, from data generation and extraction to analysis, interpretation, and use for decision-making. The course emphasizes application of nationally relevant digital systems to monitor health commodities availability and supply chain performance.
courses.duration: This course will be conducted in five days with a total of 30 contact hours. 2.3 Course objectives By the end of this course, trainees will be able to: Describe data sources across the health supply chain and their roles in supporting commodity availability and service delivery.
courses.learning_outcomes: . After completing this short course, the trainee will be able to Identify data sources across the health supply chain Evaluate the functional interrelationship between health commodity flows and quantitative supply chain data Appraise current digital platforms and technologies used for health supply chain data management and analytics Analyze essential logistics and supply chain data for informed decision-making at local and national levels. Apply health supply chain performance indicators and metrics to identify bottlenecks and opportunities for system optimization. Demonstrate value for data-driven decision-making in strengthening health supply chains. Adopt ethical, accurate, and timely data practices in health supply chain management. Embrace continuous performance monitoring and system improvement as an integral professional responsibility.

courses.title: FINANCING AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT IN HEALTH SUPPLY CHAIN
courses.source_title: FINANCING AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT IN HEALTH SUPPLY CHAIN
courses.summary: This five-day short course is designed to build a strong understanding of financing and financial management principles as they apply to health supply chains. The course focuses on how financial strategies, tools, and decision-making processes support the equitable, efficient, and sustainable availability of health commodities within health systems. Trainees will explore key concepts in health commodity financing, budgeting, costing, financial planning, and resource allocation, with an emphasis on real-world application.
courses.duration: This course will be conducted for five days Course objectives The course aims to equip trainees with a clear understanding of key concepts and principles of financing and financial management within health supply chains. It seeks to strengthen participants’ ability to identify and analyze sources and mechanisms of financing for health commodities at both national and sub-national levels.
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of the course, trainees will be able to: Explain key concepts related to the financing and financial management of health commodities within health systems. Identify major sources of financing for health commodities at national and sub-national (institutional and facility) levels, including public, donor, and pooled financing mechanisms. Analyze common financing and financial management challenges affecting health commodities availability in different health system contexts Assess the effects of different financing mechanisms and financial management practices on the availability, affordability, efficiency, and equity of health commodities. Design sustainable and context-appropriate financing strategies for health commodities that are aligned with national policies, institutional priorities, and Universal Health Coverage (UHC) goals. Evaluate financial risks, inefficiencies, and accountability gaps within health commodity supply chains and propose practical measures to improve value for money and financial performance. Training will encompass different teaching methodologies to enable trainees to apply acquired skills in health supply chain settings.

courses.summary: In order to promote evidence-based decision-making in health systems, the Introduction to Health Data Analytics course offers fundamental information and useful skills for comprehending, managing, and utilising health data. Using real-world examples from the Tanzanian health context, the course introduces learners to health systems and health data sources, fundamental statistics, data management concepts, data governance, and data analysis and visualisation. Additionally, the course introduces students to new data science methods, including the principles of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) as they apply to health.
courses.duration: The course is expected to take 5 full days to complete, with 8 hours per day, making a total of 40 hours.
courses.target_audience: Health professionals, health managers, ICT staff, researchers, students and graduates with basic quantitative skills and interest in health data use.
courses.learning_outcomes: . By the end of the course, participants will be able to: Explain key concepts and principles of health data analytics, including types of health data, data sources, and the role of analytics in strengthening health systems. Identify and describe common digital health data systems and tools used in health facilities and public health programs. Apply basic data management practices, including data cleaning, validation, and quality assurance for health data. Perform basic descriptive data analysis using appropriate analytical tools to summarise and explore health data. Interpret and communicate analytical results using tables, charts, and simple visualisations to support routine reporting and decision-making. Demonstrate awareness of ethical, legal, and governance considerations related to health data use, privacy, and security. Use health data analytics to support evidence-based decision-making at facility and program levels.

courses.summary: Key and vulnerable populations health research and programming short course is a 5 days training program designed to strengthen human resources engaged in key and vulnerable populations (KVP) research and service provision in the context of HIV epidemic. Participants come together for a training workshop where they gain knowledge and skills needed for engaging KVP in research and service provision. This short course was developed by Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences (MUHAS) in collaboration with University of Dodoma (UDOM), and University of Oslo (UiO) with funding support from the Strengthening Doctoral Education for Health in Tanzania (DOCEHTA) project.
courses.duration: The duration of the course is five (5) days with 8 hours of interaction per day, making a total of 40 contact hours.
courses.target_audience: Postgraduate students and researchers with interest in KVP research Individuals working in HIV prevention programs (NGO employees and civil servants) Health care providers in HIV services
courses.learning_outcomes: . At the end of the course, participants will be able to explain historical and theoretical perspectives related to KVP; describe how marginalization, stigma, and discrimination affect access to HIV services among KVP; design and implement HIV prevention programming tailored to KVP; apply effective community engagement strategies among KVP; and conduct of research in KVP communities.

courses.title: MANUSCRIPT BOOTCAMP
courses.source_title: MANUSCRIPT BOOTCAMP
courses.school: School of Public Health and Social Sciences
courses.summary: In today's rapidly evolving research landscape, academic work must transcend the confines of traditional theses and dissertations to engage with the wider scientific community. Although a thesis or dissertation is a comprehensive scholarly effort, its current form often requires significant transformation to meet the rigorous standards of journal publication. Recognizing this critical gap, this manuscript bootcamp is designed to empower junior faculty and postgraduate students to convert their extensive research work into a polished, journal-ready manuscript.
courses.duration: 5 days comprising of 30 hours of learning 2.3 Course objectives To identify and comprehend the essential components and structure of a manuscript To gain clarity and proficiency on transformation process from thesis or dissertation to journal-ready document To strengthen scientific communication skills
courses.target_audience: This short course is suitable for junior faculty, postgraduate students, and other research-oriented academic personnel across diverse disciplines, including but not limited to medicine, pharmacy, dentistry, science, social sciences, and allied health fields. It is specifically designed for individuals who have completed or are in the process of completing a thesis or dissertation and are ready to transform their academic work into a journal-ready manuscript. The required minimum qualification is a Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field from a recognized institution, accompanied by active engagement in academic research.
courses.learning_outcomes: By completion, participants will learn to critically analyze and reframe comprehensive research texts into structured, targeted narratives that meet the rigorous requirements of academic journals. Through a combination of didactic lectures, interactive discussions, hands-on practice, and personalized mentorship, learners will acquire strategies for clear and effective scientific communication, master the nuances of manuscript formatting and submission guidelines, and develop the confidence needed to navigate the publishing process. Ultimately, every participant will complete the bootcamp with a full first draft of a manuscript, equipping them with a solid foundation for further refinement and successful publication.
courses.certificate_awarded: ful completion of the course activities and submission of the draft manuscript, participants will receive an electronic certificate of completion, acknowledging their development and readiness to engage in the scholarly publication process.

courses.title: MASTERING INVENTORY CONTROL AND LOGISTICS FOR HEALTH COMMODITIES
courses.source_title: MASTERING INVENTORY CONTROL AND LOGISTICS FOR HEALTH COMMODITIES
courses.summary: This five-day short course aims to build capacity and improve the practical skills of in-service supply chain personnel in inventory control and distribution of health commodities. It focuses on effective store and stock management, and efficient distribution from main stores to service delivery points to ensure uninterrupted availability of health commodities. The course emphasizes the use of inventory control approaches such as just in time, min-max control system, Always, Better, Control-Vital, Essential, Desirable (ABC-VED), first expiries-first out (FEFO), first in, first out (FIFO), and re-order point to reduce stock-outs, minimize expiries, and improve transparency and accountability.
courses.duration: This course will be conducted for five days with a total of 30 contact hours and 10 hours of self-learning Course objectives This course is designed to provide participants with the knowledge and skills required for effective store management, inventory control, and health commodities distribution within the facility. Additionally, trainees will learn how to critically analyze inventory data, identify the root causes of supply chain challenges such as stock-outs, overstocking, and product expiri
courses.target_audience: Eligibility Eligible participants include: Pharmaceutical personnel Nurses with supply chain responsibilities Medical practitioners with supply chain responsibilities Laboratory technologist with supply chain responsibilities Program Officers managing health commodities (e.g., HIV, TB, malaria, vaccines) Participants should have a background in the mentioned professions or be currently employed in a healthcare facility, warehouse, program, or health-related institution, and actively involved in health commodity management. Application procedures Participants will apply directly to the Department of Pharmaceutics and Pharmacy Practice, School of Pharmacy-MUHAS. The course coordinator will leverage social media, including Instagram and WhatsApp, the MUHAS Website, and hard-copy materials suc
courses.learning_outcomes: On successful completion of this course, the trainees will be able to: Explain key inventory management strategies used in healthcare supply chains, including stock control systems and distribution models. Describe principles of warehouse and store management that ensure safe storage, quality assurance, and accountability of health commodities. Apply appropriate inventory techniques, including minimum–maximum levels and FEFO, to maintain optimal stock levels. Organize warehouse and store operations, including receiving, put-away, storage, picking, and issuing of health commodities. Implement effective health commodity distribution practices to ensure timely and secure delivery to service delivery points. Demonstrate accountability, ethical behavior, and attention to detail in inventory management and stock control activities. COURSE DESCRIPTION AND CONDUCT Course purpose This short course aims to equip trainees with comprehensive knowledge and practical skills in store and inventory management for health commodities. The course focuses on building participants’ capacity to effectively plan, manage, control, and distribute stocks using appropriate inventory control techniques such as Min–Max, ABC-VED analysis, FEFO, FIFO, and re-order point approaches. courses.title: One Health Approach in Pandemic Preparedness and Response in Tanzania
courses.source_title: One Health Approach in Pandemic Preparedness and Response in Tanzania
courses.school: Directorate of Continuing Education and Professional Development
courses.summary: This short course provides an in-depth exploration of the One Health Approach, emphasizing the interconnectedness of human, animal, and environmental health in tackling emerging and re-emerging public health threats. With a particular focus on pandemic preparedness and response, the course equips participants with both theoretical knowledge and practical skills necessary for effective disease surveillance, risk communication, and multisectoral collaboration. Through a multidisciplinary lens, participants will analyse real-world case studies from Tanzania, Africa, and the global stage, learning how integrated health systems can enhance resilience and adaptability.
courses.duration: The course is structured to be conducted intensively in five days, providing a concentrated and immersive learning experience. Course objectives Introduce the One Health concept and its relevance to pandemic preparedness and response.
courses.target_audience: This course is open to individuals and group of people from various disciplines relevant to One Health, public health, and policy development. Eligible participants must meet the following criteria: Health Professionals – Must have a background in human, animal, or environmental health, including medical practitioners, veterinarians, pharmacists, and environmental health officers. Public Health Officers – Should have prior experience in disease surveillance, outbreak response, or health system management.
courses.learning_outcomes: . By the end of the course, participants develop competencies in; Understanding of the One Health approach in pandemic preparedness and response. Understand of coordination structures and tools used for pandemic preparedness and response. Applying joint risk assessment and surveillance technique and tools effectively. Applying the multi-sectoral collaboration and policy advocacy in Tanzania. COURSE DESCRIPTION AND CONDUCT Course purpose The purpose of this short course is to equip participants with interdisciplinary competencies to design, implement, and advocate for One Health approach in pandemic preparedness and response. By integrating human, animal, and environmental health perspectives, the course aims to: Strengthen multisectoral collaboration among stakeholders in Tanzania’s health system. Enhance practical skills in joint risk assessment, surveillance, and coordination. Foster a culture of proactive health security through case-based learning and real-world simulations. courses.title: SPIROMETRY
courses.source_title: SPIROMETRY
courses.summary: Spirometry is a technique for lung function assessment. It is central to the diagnosis and management of various respiratory conditions. This short course aims to improve knowledge and skills in spirometric assessment to enhance the quality of diagnosis and management of respiratory conditions such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
courses.duration: The course will run for a maximum of one week. 2.3 Course Objectives To understand the principles of spirometry and respiratory mechanics.
courses.target_audience: 2.7.1 Eligibility Criteria: The course is designed for individuals who meet the following criteria: Healthcare professionals (doctors, nurses, clinical officers, respiratory therapists) who perform or interpret spirometry in their practice. Undergraduate and postgraduate students in medical, nursing, or allied health sciences programs with an interest in pulmonary function testing. Biomedical engineers and technicians involved in the maintenance and calibration of spirometry equipment.
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of this course, participants will have the competency to perform spirometry according to ATS/ERS standards, accurately interpret results, recognize normal and abnormal respiratory patterns, conduct pre- and post-bronchodilator testing, and effectively communicate findings for better patient management.

courses.title: SPORTS CARDIOLOGY
courses.source_title: SPORTS CARDIOLOGY
courses.summary: 1.3 Course overview Sports cardiology is an emerging subspecialty focusing on cardiovascular care of athletes and highly active individuals. Participation in sports and regular exercise is associated with substantial health benefits; however, intense exercise may unmask underlying cardiovascular disease and increase the risk of exercise-related cardiovascular events in susceptible individuals. The increasing participation in competitive sports, recreational exercise, and organized athletic activities in Tanzania and East Africa has created a growing need for healthcare professionals with competencies in sports cardiology.
courses.duration: Three (3) months comprising: One-month online learning One-month face-to-face teaching and practical demonstrations One month supervised practical attachment and field placement
courses.target_audience: This course is suitable for: Physicians Cardiologists Sports medicine physicians Internal medicine specialists Emergency medicine physicians Family medicine physicians
courses.learning_outcomes: . At completion of this course, participants will be able to: Perform cardiovascular screening of athletes using contemporary guidelines. Understand the cardiovascular adaptations to exercise and differentiate physiological athlete’s heart from pathological conditions. Perform and interpret cardiovascular diagnostic procedures relevant to sports cardiology. Evaluate symptomatic athletes presenting with chest pain, syncope, palpitations, or exercise intolerance. Correctly interpret athlete-specific ECG/ECHO findings. Identify cardiovascular conditions associated with sudden cardiac death in athletes. Make appropriate recommendations regarding sports participation and return-to-play. Participate effectively in multidisciplinary athlete care. Apply evidence-based principles in sports cardiology practice.
courses.certificate_awarded: Participants who successfully complete the course will receive a certificate of successful completion and CPD credits.

The African Region contributes the least to the cause of this crisis, yet it bears the greatest burden of suffering. Climate change has already caused significant health impacts through extreme weather and natural disasters like bushfires, floods, and mosquito-borne diseases such as malaria and dengue.
